acceptance.given: The native Toolchain command identity exists before repair work begins.

oracle.expected: A before/after native-command identity comparison reports the same identity after repair.
forbidden: Changing native command identity during repair.
oracle.observable: The repair-phase identity comparison artifact records matching native command identity values before and after the operation.

acceptance.when: Repair work is evaluated using the declared before/after native-command identity comparison.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the native-command preservation check against a repair fixture whose post-repair command identity differs from its baseline identity.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve native command identity and expose a deterministic before/after identity comparison during repair evaluation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No native command identity or command-contract migration is permitted.

slice_hint.state_transition: native command identity before repair -> identical native command identity after repair
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The repair comparison confirms that the native command identity is unchanged; an identity difference fails the preservation check.

acceptance.given: Toolchain inspection is performed against effective inspected content and evidence is about to be recorded as successful.

oracle.expected: Successful evidence is bound to the effective inspected content actually inspected.
forbidden: Successful evidence is unbound from effective inspected content.
Successful evidence is bound to content other than the effective inspected content.
oracle.observable: The successful evidence record identifies the effective inspected content identity and the inspection result bound to it.

acceptance.then: Successful evidence is associated with the effective inspected content.
acceptance.when: The supported Toolchain package route records evidence as successful after inspection.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the successful-evidence case with evidence bound to a different effective-content identity than the inspected content.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Bind every successful inspection evidence record to the identity of the effective inspected content.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing supported VDD and Acceptance routes remain available; evidence records gain no acceptance path for unbound content.

slice_hint.state_transition: inspection of effective content with pending evidence -> successful evidence bound to that effective content
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A successful evidence record names and matches the effective inspected-content identity; a missing or mismatched binding is rejected.

acceptance.given: A Candidate Route was disabled or rolled back; its approval and identity are current and bound; an applicable declared Consumer is available.

oracle.expected: The Consumer's re-enable receipt binds the current approved Candidate identity, records an actual Candidate Route invocation, and captures that invocation's current result.
forbidden: A stale or unapproved Candidate identity is invoked.
A re-enable receipt lacks an actual Candidate invocation.
A re-enable receipt lacks the current invocation result.
oracle.observable: The isolated re-enable/skip-fixture execution receipt and recorded Consumer call.

acceptance.then: The Candidate Route has been re-enabled through the Consumer and its current result is recorded.
acceptance.when: The Consumer executes re-enable after disable or rollback.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the re-enable skip fixture through the real Consumer surface; the selector must fail when no current approved Candidate invocation receipt and current result are produced.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add Toolchain re-enable dispatch that verifies the current approved Candidate identity, invokes that Candidate Route through the Consumer after disable or rollback, and emits a receipt containing the actual invocation and its captured current result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay receipt compatibility; reverting restores the prior replay dispatch without treating a configuration change or skipped call as a completed re-enable.

slice_hint.state_transition: Disabled or rolled-back Candidate Route with current bound approval and identity -> Consumer invokes the current Candidate Route -> receipt records the invocation and current result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Re-enable succeeds only if the Consumer receipt contains the current approved Candidate identity, an actual Candidate Route invocation, and that invocation's current result; otherwise the transition fails.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain verdict is pending evaluation with its source identity and execution record available for inspection.

oracle.expected: The verdict is traceable to current source identity and real execution evidence, with no assistant prose serving as authoritative evidence.
forbidden: Assistant prose is used as the sole or authoritative basis for a verdict.
A verdict is accepted without source or execution evidence.
oracle.observable: The validation inspects the verdict artifact and its referenced current source identity and execution evidence during acceptance evaluation.

acceptance.then: The verdict is evidence-based and independent of assistant prose.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain acceptance selector evaluates whether a verdict may be accepted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate a verdict lacking current source identity or real execution evidence and require acceptance validation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require the Toolchain verdict artifact to bind current source identity and real execution evidence, excluding assistant prose as an evidentiary authority.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema change; revert removes only the Toolchain verdict-evidence enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: unevaluated verdict -> verdict accepted only with inspectable source and execution evidence
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Acceptance evaluation can inspect current source identity and real execution evidence for the verdict and rejects prose-only or evidence-free verdicts.
